title: Druski Sings His Way Through His First Night Hosting 'SNL'
summary:
Comedian Druski hosted Saturday Night Live for the first time on Saturday night, and he hit all the right notes, literally. The show's musical guest was The Strokes, but it was Druski crooning 'she said yes' at just the right comedic moment that became the real earworm of the night.

Two of the funniest sketches showed off his knack for musical comedy, and some real vocal talent. In 'Proposal,' cast member Jeremy Culhane plays a man asking his girlfriend, played by Sarah Sherman, to marry him. Things do not quite go as planned. But since he assumed she would say yes, he went all-out to make the proposal an unforgettable moment, including hiring entertainment.

'I don't really know how to tell you this, but the next four minutes are about to be really tough,' Culhane says when Sherman turns him down.

And then the show goes on anyway. All eyes, and ears, turn to Druski and an ensemble that keeps growing around him as he belts with soul: 'She said yes, oh, she said yes / Can't wait to see her wearing that dress / Got down on one knee and she said yes.'

The second standout sketch, 'Golden Age of Hip-Hop,' had the Druski-led crew performing songs with titles like 'Gangs Ain't Good (Free Yo Mind)' and 'You Can Be My Brother, Friend.'

When Druski was announced as a host for the show's 52nd season, he got plenty of support from his hip-hop friends. Among those sending congratulatory comments were Drake, Travis Scott, Quavo and Wheezy.

For a first-time host, Druski showed he could do more than tell jokes. He could carry a tune, lead a growing choir of singers, and turn an awkward moment into the funniest song of the night.
why_it_matters: Live comedy shows let performers try new things in front of an audience, and this story shows how music and jokes together can turn an awkward moment into the funniest part of the night.
